summary: The root نفي primarily means to banish, exile, or send away. It also conveys the sense of denying, negating, or rejecting something, making it non-existent or invalid.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.gloss: He drove away, expelled, or banished, him, or it

parts.t: He drove away, expelled, or banished, him, or it.

headwords.def: نَفَاهُ He drove away, expelled, or banished, him, or it. (T, in TT.)

headwords.gloss: This precludes the co-existence of this therewith; is inconsistent; incompatible, with this

parts.t: This precludes the co-existence of this therewith; is inconsistent,

headwords.def: هٰذَا يُنَافِىهٰذَا This precludes the co-existence of this therewith; is inconsistent, or incompatible, with this.

headwords.gloss: It was negative; He denied a thing

parts.t: meaning an accusation or the like: syn.

headwords.def: اِنْتَفَى It was negative: contr. of ثَبَتَ and and وَجَبَ . (IbrD.) اِنْتَفَى مِنْ شَىْءٍ He denied a thing; meaning an accusation or the like: syn. تَنَضَّحَ .

headwords.gloss: Refuse; what one rejects; because of its badness

parts.t: of a thing: (M, K:) or, accord. to IAar,

headwords.def: نُفَايَةٌ Refuse; i. e. what one rejects, of a thing, because of its badness: (S:) or refuse little in quantity: (T:) or the remains, and bad portion, of a thing: (M, K:) or, accord. to IAar, what is bad of wheat or food. (M.)

headwords.gloss: A verb rendered negative; contr. of; A denied sentence; contr. of
headwords.def: فِعْلٌ مَنْفِىٌّ A verb rendered negative by its being preceded by مَا or the like; contr. of مُثْبَتٌ and مُوجَبٌ . كَلاَمٌ مَنْفِىٌّ A denied sentence; contr. of مُثْبَتٌ and مُوجَبٌ ; virtually the same as كَلاَمٌ نَافٍ a denying, or negative, sentence.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
